newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks bounce higher at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks bounce higher at close.

text.p: Fueled by oil stocks, Argentina's bolsa rallied to close at session highs Tuesday and was seen keeping a strong tone.
"The market looks good although there's still sort of puny volume," said Christopher Ecclestone of Interacciones brokers.
Oil stocks were the main feature of the day in keeping with the rise in world crude prices triggered by U.S. military action against Iraq.
The blue-chip MerVal index rose 1.7 percent to end at 518.78 while oil companies YPF, the market bellwether, and Astra jumped 2.6 percent and 2.4 percent, respectively.

"I think the market will push higher at least until Thursday, with a near-term technical target of 540," said Jorge Bonnano at Interfin brokers. "There are signs the much-awaited change of trend may be happening, although first we need to clear Friday's hurdle of (U.S.) jobs data."
The jobs report was seen as key indicator of whether the U.S. Federal Reserve will mull interest rate hikes this month.
On the local front Bonanno said investors were hopeful the government would finally take the bull by the horns and push through deep economic reforms, including changes in labor regulations.
"August tax revenue was decent and second-quarter GDP growth (of 3.2 percent) was in line with expectations -- it all helps create a micro-climate of positive expectations," Bonnano said.
But analysts did not rule out a drop in industrial activity in August after the shock replacement of former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo July 29.

"July was looking strong on the economic side. There have been no numbers since then, but there have been folk tales from people like retailers and service stations saying July was looking good and then August plunged," said Ecclestone.
August deflation of 0.1 percent in consumer prices and 0.3 percent in wholesale prices, released after the bolsa close, could feed worries over the pace of economy recovery.

In the session floor volume was extremely weak at 12 million pesos, although it surged from a nominal 2.4 million traded Monday during the U.S. Labor Day holiday. Over-the-counter deals totalled 75.9 million pesos compared to 7.7 million Monday.
"In July and August the private pension funds have been stashing away into fixed-term deposits and bonds, not putting a cent into the bolsa," said Ecclestone.

"But they've got enormous amounts of money flying in...(and) if there is a point the locals start to feel bullish about the economy then they may return and move the market the way they want to," he added.
The bolsa's broad market closed up 1.6 percent, with winners beating losers 35 to six and 20 stocks closing unchanged.
Top main-tier performers were Bansud and foods giant Molinos, both up 4.0 percent, while pulp and paper maker Celulosa and carmaker Ciadea both shed 4.0 percent.
